attempted_axis: Tooling (no source edit): add an advisory dead-strip screen to tools/gdl/datadiff.py that warns when a TU defines a local (static) data symbol with no incoming relocation in its own object - the object-level-invisible signature behind the game/ui/message.c flip failure.

attributes.law_screen: claim.law.base-cast-reconstruction-deadstrips-sibling-statics.20260831.v1 APPLIED - it is the specification for this check; its stated signature (a static datum no relocation points at, invisible to fndiff/claimcheck/datadiff because all three read the OBJECT where the siblings are still present) is implemented literally, and its prescribed fix (merge the tiled statics into ONE aggregate) is quoted in the warning text. claim.law.section-anchor-reloc-hides-symbol-liveness.20260831.v1 APPLIED - authored during this work; it supplies the opacity rule that made the check sound. claim.law.walked-base-symbol-identity.20260830.v1 SCREENED, related but not applicable: it governs WHICH of two overlapping symbols a reference should name, not whether a symbol is referenced at all. claim.law.single-base-relocation-refutes-symbol-separation.20260831.v1 SCREENED and directly relevant as context - it establishes that one relocated base plus immediate adds is a legitimate and common target shape, which is precisely the shape that makes symbol-level liveness unreadable and forced the opacity rule. No matching/codegen laws applicable: this attempt edits no C and changes no generated code.
attributes.residual: Known and documented limitation, not a defect to retry: a TU that addresses all its local data off one section anchor (`...data.0`) cannot be screened at all, because the selecting displacement lives in the ADDR16_HA/LO instruction immediates rather than the relocation addend. Closing that would require decoding those immediates out of the section bytes and re-resolving them - feasible, but it turns a relocation-table read into a disassembly pass, and the base-cast shape this screens for always produces a symbol-specific reference anyway (that is why test 2 still passes). Left as a false-negative class, stated in the tool docstring and in the section-anchor law.
attributes.scope: tools/gdl/datadiff.py only (+179/-3). New: obj_symbols(), obj_reloc_refs(), deadstrip_check(); flags --deadstrip (screen only, also accepts a direct .o path) and --no-deadstrip (suppress); the screen runs advisory inside check_unit by default. No src/*.c touched; worker owns no game TU.
attributes.verification: THREE TESTS, all green. (1) message.c FIXED state -> quiet ('every local data symbol is relocated against'). This is the real regression control: it also proves the check does NOT false-positive on the `@1` SCROLL_A literal, which is reached only through a `...rodata.0` section-alias relocation and which a name-only check would wrongly flag - the exact literal the parent law reports as lost. (2) SYNTHETIC reproduction (build/scratch/deadstrip_repro.c, compiled with the real GC/1.2.5 mwcceppc at message.c's cflags): three statics tiling one blob reached through a cast of the first; the screen flags sib_fonts (.data+0x18) and sib_cfg (.data+0x2C) and correctly spares blob_base, which the cast relocates against. It also correctly distinguishes OUTGOING relocations from incoming ones - the `...rodata.0+0x..` string pointers physically sit inside sib_fonts, and counting those as references would have hidden the very symbol under test. (3) FALSE-POSITIVE SWEEP over all 194 Matching units: 0 warnings, 194 OK. The first implementation warned on 28 of 194; diagnosing sndvoice.c produced the section-anchor law and the opacity rule that removed all 28 without losing test (2). Advisory discipline honoured: every path returns exit 0 on warnings; only real byte mismatches still set exit 1. Regression-checked the pre-existing byte-diff path (datadiff game/ui/message under --no-deadstrip still reports its three sections OK). `git diff --check` clean. The one flake8 E127 in the file is pre-existing (dol_read's zip continuation), not introduced here.
